markdown_report:
The next experiment should be a minimal lexical-residual HSTU, conditional on restoring executable training. This is a provisional selection: user simulation produced no observations, and the quantitative diagnosis contains only a subprocess failure. Consequently, no idea can satisfy the required evidence of addressing two observed user failures and one measured model failure. Earlier inspirations’ failure descriptions cannot substitute for this trial’s missing diagnosis.

**Insights and directions.** Three starting-point insights guide the experiment: shared text parameters could transfer interaction supervision between items; tying effective embeddings across histories and candidates keeps their representations consistent; conservative residual scaling limits disruption to the corrected HSTU initialization. These are mechanisms to test, not demonstrated improvements.

Three literature insights define alternatives. [HSTU-BLaIR](https://kdd2025llm4ecommerce.github.io/assets/accepted/13_HSTU_BLaIR_Lightweight_Cont.pdf) provides precedent for additive content enrichment, but its pretrained review-based encoder is prohibited here. The [HSTU reference configuration](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/configs/ml-1m/hstu-sampled-softmax-n128-final.gin) motivates objective experiments without changing backbone. The [HSTU paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.17152v3) motivates temporal biases, conditional on timestamps being available consistently during inference.

| Direction | Atomic experiment | Main uncertainty |
|---|---|---|
| Representation sharing | Scratch pooled-text residual | Sparse supervision may learn weak lexical shortcuts |
| Ranking objective | Uniform sampled-softmax replacement | Temperature and negative count require calibration |
| Temporal context | Bucketed elapsed-time attention bias | Predictor may not receive timestamps |

**Candidate assessments.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each out of 10; alignment is unavailable rather than assigned invented scores.

- **Lexical residual: 3/7/NA/NA/5.** Established fusion limits originality; shared lexical learning offers useful transfer. A localized change is feasible, although serialization and effective-embedding interfaces require care.
- **Sampled softmax: 2/6/NA/NA/4.** Standard methodology limits novelty; stronger candidate competition may improve ranking. Implementation is compact, but sampler probabilities and temperature can introduce errors.
- **Temporal bias: 3/6/NA/NA/6.** Established HSTU machinery offers a plausible recency mechanism. Temporal preferences could matter, but timestamp routing complicates implementation and deployment.

**Provisional choice.** At 10% progress, retain the lexical experiment and change only the item representation. Two prospective user concerns are overly broad thematic recommendations and missed identifier or format distinctions; a prospective model concern is incorrect positive–negative ordering. None is established by the current diagnosis.

First obtain the original training exception; the supplied traceback does not identify its cause. Preserve baseline parameters, training behavior, and random-number state when adding the lexical module. Train one network per category using shared ID-plus-text embeddings. Evaluate exclusively through pinned macro validation HR@10. Retain diagnostic interfaces, final-nonpadding readout, and identical checkpoint/predictor definitions. Report diagnostic outcomes before claiming failure-mode alignment or improvement.

idea.description: Provisional experiment: add a compact, jointly trained pooled-title/description residual to the corrected HSTU item embedding. Use the identical effective embedding for histories and candidate scoring, with one trained checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: At early research progress, a localized representation change offers a controlled test of interaction-supervised lexical sharing. It could address broad thematic matches and missed identifier or format distinctions, and reduce positive–negative ranking errors. These are prospective hypotheses: the supplied user diagnosis has no observations, and the model diagnosis reports execution failure without measured behavior. No diagnosis-qualified best idea can currently be selected.
idea.implementation_notes: The corrected baseline source and underlying training exception are absent, so a reliable executable train.py patch cannot be reconstructed from this input. Restore the baseline using the actual exception before attributing failure to any architectural component. Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per completed epoch, single-GPU execution, supplied splits, optimizer, objective, and checkpoint schedule. Save artifacts beneath the trial directory and charge all attempts to the shared budget. Use only permitted public titles/descriptions and training interactions. Construct the full corrected baseline first; initialize added parameters inside an isolated RNG context without reinitializing baseline weights. Use deterministic category-local tokenization and vocabulary, 32-dimensional randomly initialized token embeddings, masked field means, and a bias-free projection to the HSTU item width. Define effective embeddings as ID plus tanh(alpha) times a scale-matched lexical vector, with alpha initialized to zero. A zero gate initially blocks lexical-encoder gradients; the gate can learn first and subsequently activate that branch. Missing text and padding receive exactly zero residual. Preserve any baseline embedding multiplier at its original location. Deduplicate requested IDs for efficient differentiable text computation; never train through detached catalog caches. Expose effective item_emb.forward and effective weight access, log2feats(sequence), and predict_score(features, items). Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and metrics with definitions. Measure ranking errors using actual model scores and effective embeddings; mark unavailable observations unavailable. Use the greatest nonpadding sequence index, with the supplied empty-history policy. Serialize architecture, lexical assets, scale, and weights together; update the predictor writer with the same definitions and verify score equivalence after loading. Select only through the fixed macro validation HR@10; do not combine independently trained scores or checkpoints.
idea.pseudocode:
retain supplied corrected HSTU training and predictor code
obtain original exception and restore executable baseline
for category in FOUR_REQUIRED_CATEGORIES:
    load supplied data using os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']
    preserve preprocessing_seed=0 and training_seed=42
    model = construct_corrected_HSTU_in_original_initialization_order()
    with isolated_rng_state():
        lexical = scratch_text_encoder(permitted_titles_and_descriptions)
        alpha = trainable_scalar(initial_value=0)
    replace item lookup with shared effective lookup:
        id_vector = original_lookup(items)
        text_vector = lexical(items)
        text_direction = text_vector / clamp(norm(text_vector), min=epsilon)
        residual = tanh(alpha) * detach(norm(id_vector)) * text_direction
        zero residual for missing text and padding
        effective = id_vector + residual
        zero effective padding rows
    preserve baseline optimizer and objective
    for epoch in range(min(configured_epochs, 200)):
        for step in range(200):
            _, sequence, positive, negative = family_specific_sample_batch()
            features = model.log2feats(sequence)
            loss = baseline_loss_using_model_predict_score(features, positive, negative)
            baseline_optimizer_step(loss)
        execute supplied validation/checkpoint schedule
        obey supplied stopping rule
    save one selected checkpoint including lexical assets and architecture
write embedded predictor using identical architecture and category routing
verify loaded scores on left-padded sequences and missing-text cases
# Final readout: max index where sequence != 0; never nonpadding_count - 1.
# Host computes fixed macro validation HR@10; no score fusion.

originality.positive: A controlled scratch-text adaptation tests content sharing within the required HSTU family and data restrictions.
originality.negative: Additive content fusion, pooled token encoders, and gated residuals are established methods.

future_potential.positive: Verified gains could motivate inexpensive interaction-supervised lexical sharing without external weights.
future_potential.negative: Missing text, sparse supervision, and lexical shortcuts may limit transfer; current diagnostics establish no benefit.

code_difficulty.positive: The change is localized to the shared embedding module and preserves the sequential backbone.
code_difficulty.negative: Effective-weight interfaces, RNG preservation, lexical serialization, and predictor consistency require careful integration.

related_work.title: HSTU-BLaIR (2025)
contributions: Provides precedent for adding projected text representations to HSTU item representations and candidate embeddings.
limitations: Uses pretrained BLaIR representations involving reviews and metadata, which are unsuitable under this task's restrictions.
Does not establish the effectiveness of scratch-trained pooled text here.

related_work.title: HSTU sampled-softmax reference configuration
contributions: Provides an objective-focused HSTU configuration with sampled negatives, normalized representations, and temperature.
limitations: Its settings are starting points rather than validated optima for the four Amazon categories.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces the HSTU sequential-transduction family and relative positional and temporal attention mechanisms.
limitations: Does not establish that temporal modification improves this fixed benchmark.
Temporal extensions require consistent observed-prefix timestamp availability in training and prediction.
